mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4-quarter rise in real GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.5% signals accelerating economic expansion, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% for four consecutive quarters but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals labor market tightness, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as wage pressures boost corporate margins.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 4.0% for three consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 1.0% signals improved manufacturing activity, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as supply chain constraints ease.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises above 1.0% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 1.2 million units signals weakening residential construction activity, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as housing sector earnings prospects deteriorate.
failure_condition: If HOUST falls below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as higher borrowing costs depress corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 5.0% for one month but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.0% signals labor market weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending declines.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 6.0% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month rise in the retail sales index (RSAFS) above 5.0% signals accelerating consumer spending, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as retail sector earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: If RSAFS rises above 5.0% for one month but S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 0.5% signals manufacturing weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as supply chain disruptions persist.
failure_condition: If INDPRO falls below 0.5% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
